blindSummary: This country presents serious risk for trans visitors despite same-sex conduct being legal: an LGBTQ-rights news outlet documents that anti-gay lynchings are commonplace, and a community support organisation provides safe housing for LGBT youth fleeing family violence. There is no legal gender recognition and no anti-discrimination law; the community organises underground.
blindOutOfScope: The lynching pattern is a documented social climate, not statute.
blindSourceSummaries: An LGBTQ-rights news outlet (April 2024): interview with the founder of a community support organisation in this country, which since 2013 has supported LGBT+ people with housing - founded after a father murdered his gay son. Nearly 380 young people from this country and the surrounding sub-region have passed through its 20-place temporary accommodation centre; the organisation now has branches in three neighbouring states. The article notes anti-gay lynchings are commonplace here.

An international LGBT-rights organisation's country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations are not criminalised in this country, but there is no SOGI discrimination protection, no legal gender recognition, and LGBTI organisations cannot register. LGBTIQ people face stigma from the public and police, which cracked down on a 'network of homosexuals' in 2022. A 2021 national human-rights commission report flagged physical and sexual assault, arbitrary detention, torture and degrading treatment against LGBTQI+ people; LBQ women rarely report violence to police.

A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report on this country: official assessment including the section on acts of violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity - same-sex conduct not criminalised but no protections; documents societal stigma and police treatment.

NOTE: page content did not load at fetch time (only an LGBTQ news site's navigation was retrieved); the underlying Aug 2015 piece features the voices of LGBT people within a major faith community in the sub-region, including in this country.

An LGBTQ-rights news outlet (May 2012): interview with an academic - same-sex relations have a long history in this region (evidence documented in several countries, including royal households' relations with pages and marriages between women in a former kingdom on this country's territory); both historic criminal laws and modern anti-discrimination activism are characterised here as foreign imports.
blindLocalsOnly: The absence of legal gender recognition and of anti-discrimination protection are resident-facing gaps; a community safe-house network serves local youth.
blindTangential: Anti-gay lynching pattern — trans people are among the most visible targets of perceived-LGBT violence; same-sex conduct itself is legal.
